newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian airline seeks foreign debt consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian airline seeks foreign debt consolidation.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-run Balkan Airlines will start talks with Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank for the consolidation of the airline's foreign debt, an airline spokesman said on Tuesday.

"The airline will seek debt restructuring to stabilise its finances before the firm is privatised, and negotiations will begin with Bayerische Vereinsbank to consolidate our foreign debt," Viktor Melamed said.
He said Balkan's debts totalled $100 million but declined to specify the size of the foreign debt within that total.

Balkan's executive director Victor Doganov said earlier this month that debt restructuring would be the first step towards the company's planned privatisation and would make it more attractive for foreign investors.
Officials said a debt-for-equity swap would ensure the German bank a stake in the airline after its sale.
Bayerische Vereinsbank holds a 51 percent stake in a joint banking institution named Bayerische Bulgarische Handelsbank, set up in 1995 with Bulgaria's state-owned Bulbank.
